digest.component_or_area: rebar CLI positional-body commands / store durability
propositions: rebar comment takes its body positionally and silently stores an option-looking token like --body-file or --body as the comment body, discarding the intended content while exiting 0.
The failure is undetectable because there is no stderr, exit code is 0, and a comment still appears so a len(comments) check passes even though the content is lost.
A second stacked defect dropped any surplus positional holding the intended value via an args[:min_args] slice, so a body passed after a flag token was lost twice over.
A body argument beginning with '-' must be rejected with a non-zero exit and a message naming the correct form, with '--' as the documented escape hatch for legitimate leading-dash bodies.
The guard must cover every positional-body command of this shape (comment, tag, untag, archive, set-verify-commands, and audit of create/edit/session-log), not just comment.
The change chose not to add a real --body-file option, documenting the shell-substitution idiom instead as the explicit decision.
